summary: Morris County, TX Texas Forest Service tower about 100 ft high, described in a 1958 federal survey and staffed in 1970; indexed as gone, with no site description found.

facts.design: Four-legged steel tower, legs bolted to concrete piers, glass windows around the top, colored gray
facts.status_note: Forest Fire Lookout Association index marks it Tower Gone; no removal date or description of the site today found

staffing.status: two-person crew assigned by Texas Forest Service; no later staffing record found

events.note: Coast and Geodetic Survey station description (1958) describes the tower, about 100 ft high, on a wooded ridge about 1.5 mi NW of Daingerfield
Naples Monitor clipping (Sept 17, 1970): two Morris County natives hired by Texas Forest Service and assigned to the Daingerfield tower; gear kept at home, on call 24 hours

notes_for_editor: Brief height (30.5 m) matches the survey's about 100 ft, so no correction. The 1970 staffing comes from a newspaper clipping reprinted on Forest Lookouts; the men are not named in the story. The tnlandforms numeric column (614) is unexplained and is not used. No build date, removal date, later staffing, or fire history found, so the story leaves those out. Budget: 2 WebSearch calls and about 6 page reads, with the state index pages shared across the three towers.
